ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Panama Law No. 23 of 2015 on AML/CFT, as amended, together with Law No. 129 of 2020 creating the National Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiarios Finales), Executive Decree No. 3 of 2022, and Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations; supervised by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), the Panamanian Public Registry, and licensed registered agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Persona Jurídica) of the corporate founder and, if applicable, of each corporate council member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of passports of all ultimate beneficial owners, including the founder, council members, and named beneficiaries where identifiable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or creditworthiness certificate addressed to the Panamanian registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution in the issuer's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or judicial background certificate for each substantial beneficial owner and signatory (for enhanced AML review)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national police or judicial authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, council members, protectors, and ultimate beneficiaries against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's domestic consolidated list maintained by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF). Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified and assessed under Law No. 23 of 2015, requiring enhanced due diligence, source of wealth verification, and escalation to the registered agent's compliance officer; all screening must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) online name search and reservation portal via Panamá Digital, available at www.panamadigital.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the statutory registry language. The foundation's distinctive name may be in any Latin-script language, but the deed and public registry order require a Spanish transliteration and must include the mandatory suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'FIP'. Names must be distinct from all existing registered corporate, foundation, and registered mark names; registration is denied for names deemed confusingly similar, deceptive, or contrary to public order.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fundación de Interés Privado (the mandatory suffix cannot be used as the distinctive name itself)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five (5) business days of a name rejection notification, the petitioner may file a recurso de reconsideración before the Directorship General of the Public Registry, attaching the original search receipt and a memorandum distinguishing the rejected name from any prior-registered mark. If the reconsideration is denied, the petitioner may file a recurso de apelación before the higher administrative instance within five (5) additional business days. The Registry must resolve the appeal within fifteen (15) business days. Judicial recourse before the Third Chamber of the Panamanian Supreme Court is available after exhaustion of administrative remedies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the legal seat only when provided through a licensed Panamanian registered agent with a physical address in the Public Registry. For the importation of deep-frozen meat and seafood under ISIC 4632, the industry authorities (Panama's Food Safety Authority, the Ministry of Health, and the National Customs Authority) require a physical business address, cold-storage capacity, HACCP registration, and sanitary import permits; a mere virtual office cannot satisfy this operational substance for import licensing and customs registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate at approximately 20% within the first 12 months for a purely passive holding foundation; elevated to approximately 55% within the first 12 months once active cold-chain import operations, customs declarations, and health permits are in place due to unannounced port, customs, and sanitary food-safety inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Panamanian notarial fee schedule; prevailing market benchmark for a simple foundation charter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration fee for inscription of the foundation charter in the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration tariff for private interest foundations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent office and compliance services (first-year service fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian registered agent (abogado or licensed trust company)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market standard annual fee for PIF maintenance (USD 1,000-1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO risk classification, KYC/AML customer onboarding, and PEP/OFAC/UN screening package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing compliance fee for a Low-Risk Standard profile under the AML/CFT regime

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of notarized UBO and good-standing documents (bundle of three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (authentication office) or Public Registry apostille section
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Panamanian fee of USD 50 per document / equivalent foreign consular fee standard

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign corporate registry documents, passports, and good-standing certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn public translator (licensed by the Panamanian Supreme Court or Ministry of Education)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately USD 25 per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foundation minute book, internal corporate records, and initial resolutions (Acta de Instalación) preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat documentation and stamped minute-book fee at prevailing market rates

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama; online tax administration portal: Sistema Integrado de Tributación (SIT) at https://sit.mef.gob.pa. Customs enforcement for import/export ITBMS is handled by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through its electronic customs declaration system, integrated with SIT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panamanian Private Interest Foundation (PIF, Ley 25 de 1995) must: (1) hold Public Registry registration of its Public Instrument of Foundation and maintain a resident agent in Panama; (2) appoint a resident legal representative and licensed CPA; (3) obtain a SIT digital signature (Firma Electrónica); (4) file Formulario de Inscripción via SIT or the DGI service center, submitting certified and Spanish-translated foundation charter, apostilled powers of attorney, Panama registered office address, and director/beneficiary identification; (5) upon approval, receive the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), which is the sole TIN/VAT number for ITBMS and income tax purposes; (6) register with ANA as importer of record for DUA filing; and (7) secure the municipal Aviso de Operación where local economic activity is conducted. The PIF also pays a flat annual foundation tax (currently B/.350) administered separately from income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama applies source-based territorial taxation. The PIF is an autonomous judicial patrimony with separate legal personality and is neither a pass-through nor a tax-exempt vehicle per se: it is taxable at entity level at the corporate income tax rates (15% on the first B/.50,000 of Panama-source taxable income and 25% above that amount) only on income derived from Panamanian sources, including import/trading margins from domestic wholesale sales of frozen beef and seafood. Foreign-source income, foreign banking deposits, and foreign-source capital gains remain exempt in Panama, giving the structure a hybrid profile for cross-border planning but no domestic pass-through election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box or CFC election system. Applicable elections include: (i) election into the small-taxpayer simplified ITBMS regime (annual gross income up to B/.200,000) with quarterly settlement; (ii) election of ITBMS refund filing frequency for exporters in a credit position; (iii) election to operate under the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime (Ley 41 de 2007) for regional service income; and (iv) election by the PIF to be constituted as a public-interest foundation (Fundación de Interés Público) for certain exempt purposes. No domestic hybrid mismatch election is available; mismatches must be managed through entity classification differences recognized in the counterpart jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panamanian value-added consumption tax collected at importation by ANA and administered by DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.200,000 (USD 200,000; balboa at 1:1 parity with USD) — annual gross income ceiling for the optional simplified ITBMS regime for small taxpayers. There is no zero-registration threshold: any person habitually selling taxable goods or services in Panama, and every importer of record, must register for the standard ITBMS regime. A reduced 2% rate applies to qualifying basic food basket items, including designated fresh/frozen meat and seafood lines, while alcoholic beverages and tobacco attract higher differential rates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance through SIT electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica): all registered taxpayers must transmit invoice XML data to DGI via the SIT web-services API and receive a DGI validation and unique Código de Autorización before the invoice is legally issued; no physical fiscal stamping is used. Import declarations (DUA) are cleared electronically through ANA's single window, with ITBMS assessed and paid at the customs edge and linked to the SIT invoice record; zero-rated export invoices must be flagged as 'Exportación' and validated online.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating (0%) applies to (i) goods physically exported from Panama to a foreign destination with evidence of effective departure, (ii) goods delivered to a licensed free zone (e.g., Colón Free Zone or Panamá Pacífico) for re-export, and (iii) services performed and enjoyed outside Panama. An exporter holding a valid RUC and ANA exporter registration may credit or refund ITBMS borne on importation of frozen beef/seafood if the same goods are subsequently exported; meat and fishery consignments additionally require MIDA/ARAP sanitary certificates.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) validated by ANA showing actual 'salida efectiva' (effective departure) of the goods
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill naming the foreign consignee and matching the declared HS codes (0202/0203 beef, 0303 pelagic fish)
Commercial export invoice and packing list reconciled with DUA quantities, weights, and Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/MT202 bank credit advice proving collection of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
SIT zero-rate e-invoice record bearing the DGI-issued Código de Autorización
MIDA/ARAP sanitary and health export certificates for meat and fishery products, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA jointly perform post-clearance document verification and audits of zero-rating claims within the statutory limitation period. Where export substantiation fails, the full ITBMS (7% standard or 2% reduced rate) is retroactively assessed with statutory surcharges and monthly moratory interest, and any refund previously paid is clawed back with interest. Fraudulent documentation exposes the PIF, its legal representative, and advisors to Código Fiscal administrative fines proportional to the tax evaded, criminal tax-fraud prosecution, loss of exporting/e-invoicing privileges, and disqualification from the simplified regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No standing central bank in Panama; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) acts as the prudential banking regulator, while Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as fiscal agent and clearing bank for the Republic; the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) oversees sovereign financial policy. The US dollar is legal tender, and the Balboa remains only a fractional coin unit pegged 1:1 to the USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system without any currency exchange control regime. There are no restrictions on capital account transactions, no current account convertibility licensing, and no profit remittance barriers for foreign investors. Dividends, interest, royalties, and trade settlements may be freely transferred abroad through the domestic banking system. The only practical hurdles are AML/CFT bank-level due diligence, documentary compliance with the SBP's know-your-customer (KYC) rules, and withholding tax obligations on Panamanian-source income as per the territorial tax code. Profits attributable to foreign-source income earned by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) are generally outside Panamanian taxation, but bank remittances must still satisfy source-of-funds evidentiary standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds in Panama. The USD is both the domestic and settlement currency; therefore no surrender, repatriation, or forced conversion obligations apply. Exporters and importers may retain proceeds in any convertible currency within the Panamanian banking system; however, banks apply internal AML compliance filters and require the underlying trade documents to support all inbound and outbound wire activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Revolving Import LC
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore and unlicensed fintech digital EMI providers are legally prohibited from operating in Panama or opening deposit accounts for local or foreign-domiciled PIFs without obtaining a banking or fintech license from the SBP under Law 1 of 2018 and Decree 239 of 2021. Feasibility is rated Low for fully non-resident digital EMIs; however, a PIF may use a licensed Panamanian fintech or multi-bank platform only for payment initiation where funds ultimately clear through SBP-regulated commercial banks. Legal constraints include mandatory AML registration, beneficial ownership disclosure, transaction monitoring, and the operational absence of a Panama-specific e-money passporting regime from the EEA or other jurisdictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the founder, the foundation council, and the beneficial owner during initial onboarding. Most first-tier Panamanian banks mandate a face-to-face interview with at least one natural person with signing authority, conducted either at the branch in Panama or, exceptionally, through an Apostilled power of attorney plus a notarized video call accepted by the bank's compliance committee. Remote-only opening for a private interest foundation is rare and typically denied where the underlying activity is import trade with real counterparties. For Medium and Low risk tiers, banks may accept certified notarized copies, legalized corporate documents, and an interview performed by a correspondent bank or a Panamanian attorney-in-fact, but final approval remains at the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation lacks transparent beneficial owner registration in the SBP's beneficial ownership database.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified copy of the foundation deed, foundation council resolution appointing beneficiary, notarized statement of beneficial ownership, valid passports, residence proofs, and Patronato registration certificate (Ficha Única) plus the current legal guardian certification from the SBP list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial capital escrow deposit is inconsistent with the foundation's stated wholesale import purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply audited corporate financial statements of the settlor, bank reference letters from remitting financial institutions, sworn declaration of lawful origin of funds, and a cash-flow projection reconciling the import cycle of ISIC 4632 frozen beef and seafood products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade payment destination involves jurisdictions perceived as high-risk by Panamanian bank compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full pro-forma invoices from frozen beef and seafood exporters, commercial contract with Incoterms, vessel or container booking confirmation, cold-chain certificates, ocean bill of lading drafts, and a risk rationale explaining why the exporter jurisdiction presents no sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually rapid activation of the import revolving letter of credit line before any transaction history exists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the PIF's corporate private placement of capital, foundation council due diligence protocol, trade transaction matrix of at least three forward supply agreements with bonded cold storage logistics contracts, and evidence of prior experience of the council members in cold-chain meat and seafood trading.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from shareholders, settlors, or direct lenders must be wired exclusively to the PIF's named commercial bank account in Panama, using SWIFT MT103 for directly held funds or MT202 for intermediary transfers. The Panamanian receiving bank will require the underlying purpose code, e.g., 'Foundation capital contribution', 'Trade working capital loan', or 'Pre-export financing', together with a capital subscription resolution or loan agreement. Funds are held in USD; wire instructions must reference the IBAN-equivalent Panamanian account number (CLABE is not used) and the bank's SWIFT/BIC. The SBP requires banks to verify the identity of the ultimate originator and perform real-time screening, so all wire references should identify the direct remitter precisely to avoid rejection. For a PIF, the minimum capital requirement under the Private Interest Foundations Law must be funded at onboarding, and any subsequent injection must be evidenced by a foundation council resolution and, if above USD 100,000, a notarized declaration of source of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for frozen beef and seafood import are best executed through: (a) commercial documentary letters of credit opened by a Panamanian first-tier bank confirmed by a correspondent bank in the exporter's jurisdiction, with settlement via SWIFT MT700/MT710/MT754 and SWIFT MT103 for reimbursement; (b) direct SWIFT MT103 transfers for pre-negotiated open-account consignments; or (c) SWIFT MT202 for cross-border nostro account settlement. The PIF should structure payments according to Incoterms such as CIF or CNF, with documentary presentation including the full set of ocean bills of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, sanitary/phytosanitary certificate, and the Banco Nacional de Panamá or Banistmo trade finance desk's stamp. For recurring shipments, a revolving LC with maximum USD 2,000,000 per tranche is recommended, subject to margin deposits and commodity-specific goods inspection reports. All LC and SWIFT instructions must include contract reference numbers and INN tariff-line descriptions to avoid AML false positives.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable forward contracts with SBP-licensed Panamanian banks where the underlying trade invoice is denominated in euros
USD/GBP deliverable forwards for payments to United Kingdom seafood processors under documented physical import sales
Cross-currency swaps between USD and major trade currencies for cold-chain wholesale receivables financing
Vanilla foreign exchange options (call/put) on USD/EUR or USD/GBP, exercised only against a verified import or sales contract
Non-deliverable forwards are not applicable in Panama due to the official parallel between USD and Balboa; no NDF market exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise fee (Gravamen Anual / Tasa Única de Mantenimiento) for the Panama Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Revenue Authority (ANIP, formerly DGI), with registry effects administered by the Registro Público of Panama through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually by 30 June of each calendar year; the US$300.00 fixed fee applies irrespective of the foundation's month of incorporation or business volume
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus 1% monthly default interest; failure to pay for more than one year causes suspension of the foundation's registration effects, and two or more consecutive unpaid years expose the PIF to administrative strike-off from the Registro Público

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Beneficial Ownership Registry of Panama administered by ANIP, with the Resident Agent acting as filing intermediary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually by 30 June, in coordination with the franchise fee cycle; each transfer or variation of the founder's reserved rights, change of Foundation Council member, or beneficiary substitution must be reported within 30 calendar days of the written amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing of materially false UBO data exposes the foundation and the Resident Agent to monetary penalties and suspension of the foundation's capacity to hold bank relationships or clear import shipments through customs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración anual de renta) for Panama-source wholesale income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Revenue Authority (ANIP) – Income Tax Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the return is due by 31 March of the following year, subject to ANIP's RUC-based instalment schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency accrues monthly default interest and late-filing fines; an outstanding return prevents issuance of the Paz y Salvo tax clearance, which in turn blocks customs release of frozen beef and seafood consignments and any act before the Registro Público

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on Panama-source taxable income for legal entities
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system; foreign-source income is excluded from the tax base. No statutory tax holiday for ISIC 4632 frozen beef/seafood import; small taxpayers may qualify for a reduced 15% rate on taxable profit up to USD 1.5 million if formally classified by the DGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Declaración Jurada del ISR para Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI electronic portal DIGITAX/T@D (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year taxpayers must file no later than 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I, Box 1 - RUC and registered name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity, RUC, domicile, resident agent, and status of the Private Interest Foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pre-register the PIF with the DGI and obtain an active RUC before filing; enter the exact foundation name as certified by the resident agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II, Box 38 - Panama-source gross income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced revenue from wholesale sale of frozen beef and seafood within Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only sales consummated in Panama; keep freight, insurance, and cold-chain documentation to evidence any foreign-resale exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II, Box 40 - Cost of sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible acquisition cost, customs duties, quarantine fees, freight, and storage costs linked to taxable Panama sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support entries with customs filings, supplier invoices, frozen logistics reports, and shipping manifests; no inflated cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part III, Box 45 - Taxable net income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Panama-source profit after authorized deductions and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only the 5-year loss carryforward schedule; foreign-source losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part IV, Box 55 - Income tax at applicable rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of 25% (or qualified 15% small-taxpayer rate) on taxable net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the precise rate and attach any DGI resolution recognizing reduced small-taxpayer status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part IV, Box 70 - Tax due / credit balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after advance payments, withholding tax credits, and prepaid corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit via ACH at Banco Nacional de Panamá before submission; file a zero declaration even when no tax is due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% per month surcharge on the unpaid tax up to 100%, plus administrative fines of USD 50 to USD 5,000. Failure to file a tax return with tax due may additionally trigger a 25% to 50% penalty on the omitted tax and suspension of the foundation's operating registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding on taxable Panama-source profits distributed by a Panamanian legal entity. Distributions by a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25/1995 are not legally characterized as dividends and generally fall outside the dividend withholding net unless they are re-characterized as Panama-source remuneration or taxable transfers.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owners claiming DTA relief must submit a written treaty-relief request to the DGI before remittance, enclosing a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) for the foreign tax year, a Form 881 declaration of beneficial ownership, the distribution or payment agreement, and evidence of actual local withholding. The DGI may grant a reduced withholding order; if excess tax has been withheld, the beneficiary must file Form 890 (Solicitud de Devolución) attaching the same evidence within the statutory refund window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid for the use of IP in Panama carry a 10% statutory WHT, subject to DTA reduction or exemption. Interest paid by a Panama taxpayer to a non-resident lender is generally subject to a 5% WHT on Panama-source interest, except for arm's-length foreign bank credit not attributable to a Panama permanent establishment, which may qualify for a 0% rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 in related-party transactions and USD 3,000,000 in consolidated annual turnover; Panama uses the US dollar as circulating legal tender, so the local-currency threshold is denominated in USD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Panamanian ESR framework applies to a legal entity conducting a relevant activity such as the import and distribution of frozen goods. The PIF must demonstrate substantial economic presence in Panama: physical premises, qualified local personnel, core income-generating activity performed in Panama, and annual expenditure adequate to its scale of operations. Failure to satisfy the ESR test entails a fine up to USD 1 million, a surcharge of twice the undeclared benefit, and potential deregistration of the foundation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and non-filing of Form 110
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panama-source frozen beef/seafood resale income, use of inflated supplier invoices, duplicate cost deductions, or systematic non-filing of annual ISR returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to USD 5,000, a 25%-50% penalty on the omitted tax, monthly late-payment surcharges, and criminal liability with imprisonment of 3 to 6 years under the Panamanian Fiscal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council members, and the resident agent may be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution, face freeze orders on personal assets, travel bans, and denial of exit permits where the foundation was used as a mere conduit for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham shell foundation and ESR failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF without local staff, premises, banking decision-making, or records; routing import profits through the foundation while all management, control, and commercial substance are located outside Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cancellation of foundation registration, revocation of tax benefits, fines up to USD 1 million under Law 201/2021, and a deficiency assessment equal to twice the undeclared taxable benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing applies: directors and officers become personally liable for cessation credits, face bans from acting as directors in any Panamanian entity for up to 10 years, and are subject to civil damages actions by creditors and third parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/invoice fraud and shadow financial engineering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing commercial import receivables through unreported Swift TT or revolving LC structures, issuing false customs or purchase invoices, and laundering profits through foundation bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Urgent freezing of assets, fines between USD 100,000 and USD 2 million under Ley 23/2015, criminal conspiracy charges with sentences up to 12 years, and seizure of the imported merchandise and the benefiting assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation protectors may be subjected to travel bans, passport revocation, and personal criminal liability; the court may also order disqualification from managing regulated activities for up to 10 years and require personal restitution of the laundered amount.
